decisions.reason: The inexact Definition imports the finite FISTA recurrences of alg-proximal-gradient-and-fista and changes only the proximal output. That exact Definition assumes convex C1 f with L-Lipschitz gradient, L>0, and proper closed convex g. Thus f=1-cos(x) is inadmissible. Under the inherited hypotheses F is convex, the certified one-step estimate applies, and expanding u_k=u_{k-1}+t_k(x_k-y_k) yields the stated error term 2t_k^2 eta_k/L. The k=1 proof uses z=x_* directly, avoiding an infinite starting objective.

The exact algorithm takes a finite budget N, whereas the theorem leaves k and j unrestricted. This is a nonfatal index-scope omission: the proof already establishes one-step and one-block contraction and then finite induction, and exact proximal uniqueness makes executions with overlapping budgets agree. The Statement now explicitly defines the compatible arbitrary-horizon sequences and states the finite-run restrictions k<=N and jm<=N, preserving both original rates and all restart points. Independently checked gap<=||r||^2/(2mu), ||r||<=2L||d||, descent L||d||^2/2, and quadratic growth, yielding q=1/(1+mu/(4L)) and the block factor 4L/(mu(m+1)^2)<=1/2.

The supplied inexact Definition explicitly says to use the finite FISTA recurrences of alg-proximal-gradient-and-fista and the same momentum update as that exact recurrence. The named exact Definition states t_1=1 and t_{j+1}=(1+sqrt(1+4t_j^2))/2, so F2 accurately unfolds a composed algorithm rather than assuming an unsupported recurrence. Telescoping the checked energy estimate, dropping ||u_k||^2, and proving (j+1)/2<=t_j<=j by induction give exactly the displayed weighted-error bound. Nonnegative eta_j justifies replacing t_j^2 eta_j by j^2 eta_j. The asymptotic assertion is conditional on a certified sequence and its weighted summability, not on the existence of an arbitrary uncertified infinite run.
